plan: Initialize cash flow model for Option A (Rent), calculating the daily burn rate (service + fuel) and tracking the balance from Day 0 through Day 42, with specific boundary checks on Day 14, 28, and 35.
Initialize cash flow model for Option B (Buy), calculating the daily burn rate (fuel only) and tracking the balance from Day 0 through Day 42, with specific boundary checks on Day 14, 28, and 35.

Initialize cash flow model for Option C (Outsource), calculating the daily burn rate (service only) and tracking the balance from Day 0 through Day 42, with specific boundary checks on Day 14, 28, and 35.
Perform a comparative analysis of the minimum cash balance reached by each option against the $2,500 minimum cash threshold to determine financial viability.
Identify and document evidence gaps regarding payment reliability and cost volatility to qualify the final decision.
evidence_to_validate: Contractual payment terms for the Day 14 and Day 35 collections to assess the risk of late payment.
Vendor service level agreements (SLAs) for the rental and outsourcing options to verify the fixed nature of daily service costs.
Fuel price indices for the specific region to validate the daily fuel cost assumptions for Options A and B.
output.method: Iterative daily balance tracking. For each day (1-42), the model will first deduct the daily operating cost and then apply any scheduled cash events. Balance checks will be performed at Day 0 (post-setup), and both pre-event and post-event for days 14, 28, and 35. The viability of each option will be determined by whether the balance ever drops below the $2,500 floor.
